newsitem.title: UK: WH Smith gains after upbeat AGM statement.
newsitem.headline: WH Smith gains after upbeat AGM statement.

text.p: Shares in WH Smith Plc rose on Wednesday after upbeat comments from the retail group to shareholders at its annual general meeting and relief that the comments contained no fresh bad news, traders and analysts said.

Chairman Jeremy Hardie said total group sales were up four percent in the four months to the end of September. He said the group's performance overall was in line with expectations and the company viewed full-year prospects with confidence.
The stock was up 10p at 465-1/2, continuing a rebound since it dropped to a four-month low of 447p on October 9.

Hardie also said the company had undertaken a restructurting of its head office involving a 30 percent cut in staff numbers. He said the company was "well placed to drive for improved profitability sales and customer service."
Yet analysts said there was nothing particularly new in the statement and said the stock may be seeing no more than a relief rally after recent negative news.
"It didn't strike me that there was anything particularly new," said Robert Snaith, analyst at SocGen. "But there is a note of confidence and a promise of cuts in head office costs."
In August WH Smith posted a pre-tax loss of 194.7 million stg, the first loss in its 204-year history, and said it still had some way to go before returning to peak profits.
